## What is verified, and where

- **The numerical core** (`hcc-core`, Rust compiled to WebAssembly) has a
  validation suite that `cargo test --release` runs on every push: the
  $n$LPT recursion through fourth order by equation-of-motion residual
  scaling in 2D and 3D, the 2LPT closed form, the exact $\Lambda$CDM growth
  tables, Hopf–Cole against the Zel'dovich sheet, the dual and P1 sheets,
  the exact clipped deposits against 70 fixtures of the Julia `R3D.jl`
  port, the deposit-free spectra, the top-hat window deconvolution, the
  viscous kernel and the phase statistics. Every claim in the text that
  rests on one of these carries a ✓ badge linking to the test.
- **The API documentation** of the core is published with the book at
  [api/hcc_core](../api/hcc_core/index.html); the ⟨name⟩ marks in the text
  link to the function that evaluates the equation next to them.
- **The WebGPU compute path** of the 3D laboratory is checked against the
  WebAssembly reference by a self-test page:
  [gpu-test.html](../app/gpu-test.html?auto=1&val=32,64) (open it in a
  WebGPU-capable browser; it reports every check).
- **Citations** were verified against the NASA ADS before entering the
  bibliography.

## Lineage

The text grew out of a lecture notebook on Fourier methods for Burgers'
equation; the notebook is included:
[solve_burgers_equation_FFT_2025.ipynb](../notebooks/solve_burgers_equation_FFT_2025.ipynb).

## How to cite

The repository carries a `CITATION.cff`; GitHub shows it as "Cite this
repository". Until a DOI is minted, cite the repository and the commit above:

```
Abel, T. (2026). Hopf–Cole Cosmology: from Burgers' equation to the cosmic web, in your browser.
https://yipihey.github.io/hopf-cole-cosmology/ (commit {{< var build.sha >}})
```

## Sharing a view of the laboratory

Every state of the laboratory is encoded in the address bar (the part after
`#`), so copying the URL shares the exact experiment, including the
smoothing scale, the seed, the viscosity and which panels are shown. The
*copy link* button does this; the preset menu lists the experiments of the
[lab guide](08-lab.qmd). Plots download as SVG or CSV from their toolbars,
field panels as PNG.

## Annotating and discussing

Pages carry the Hypothesis sidebar (top right): select any passage to
annotate it, publicly or in a private group. Corrections and questions are
welcome as [issues](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology/issues);
every page has an *Edit this page* link.
